This land is my own and I have been planting yam and cassava here for many years. Chemical fertilizer is costly and the traders here do not always bring it, so for root crops I depend on the household waste and goat droppings I gather through the dry season to mound up the yam heaps. I will plant the setts and cuttings I saved from last harvest — they do well in this soil. The work of clearing, mounding and weeding is heavy, so I will call on a few men to help with the mounds, but most of the season I manage the plot myself with my children.
